# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.41 (pre-release)

A round of changes asked for by a tester after trying the program on 67 phone photos of a book, on top of pre.40 (publish only this one). Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine. The automated test suite passes on CI runners for Linux x86-64 and arm64, Windows x86-64 and arm64, and macOS. **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**Read before upgrading**
- Defaults are unchanged: every new function is off or neutral until you use it, so without the new options the output is the same as in pre.40.
- Project files written by this version may carry new lines (`cut_angle`, `keystone`, `page_keystone` in the general settings; `cut-angle`, `keystone`, `page1.KEY`, `page2.KEY` under a sheet). Older versions skip lines they do not know, so they open such a project but **silently lose** the slanted cut, the keystone and the per-page settings.
- `page1.KEY` / `page2.KEY` refuse the keys that belong to the whole sheet (`split`, `auto_orient`, `cut_angle`, `keystone`, `dpi`) with an error naming the line; a key for a page other than 1 or 2 (`page3.…`) is skipped like any unknown key.

**New**
- **Slanted cut line** (`--cut-angle DEGREES`, ±20°): each page keeps its side of the slanted line, the other side is painted with the paper colour. In the window, a "Line lean" slider with the Cut line type; right-click on the line removes it and resets the lean.
- **Keystone correction** (`--keystone-v`, `--keystone-h`, percent, ±30): straightens a sheet photographed at an angle before the cut. In the window, two sliders in the "This page" bar.
- **Auto keystone** button (after the pages are split): measures each page (tilt of the text lines, width of the text at top and bottom) and keeps a correction for that page only (`pageN.page_keystone`). Careful on purpose: with too few lines, margins that do not mirror each other, or a drift above 6 % it leaves the page as it is. The −45°/+45° buttons stay.
- **Settings per page**: "Settings for: All pages / This page only" above Output and Clean-up (mode, threshold, despeckle and the other clean-up settings); the green content box changes only the page it is dragged on. In a project: `page1.KEY = VALUE`, `page2.KEY = VALUE`.
- **Paper sizes**: `--page-size` and the window list now include A2–A6, B3–B6, Letter, Legal and Tabloid; `WxH` in mm still works.
- **OCR pencils** on the processed pages: green (OCR zone), red (ignored area), violet (table). `--ocr-zone X,Y,W,H[=LANG]#table` reads a zone as one uniform block, row by row (Tesseract mode 6).
- **Slider view** shows both pages of a cut sheet when the original is cut.
- **Freehand guide lines** keep about a third of the nodes (smoothed, then simplified, at most 10 per line).
- Presentation site, READMEs (all languages) and the user guides (all languages) describe the new functions.

**Fixed (found by hostile testing before this release)**
- Automatic keystone first read the width of the ink in bands of the page, which on real text gave readings at the ±10 % limit for almost every page; replaced by margins read from the lines themselves, accepted only when both margins drift in opposite directions.
- `--page-size A4x`, `x` and similar now name the option and the part that is not a number, instead of "invalid float literal".
- `#table` is accepted in any letter case.

**Verified**: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and the unit and CLI tests of every crate; new hostile tests for the new functions (thousands of random images and settings with NaN, infinity, extreme angles and keystones and nested per-page settings; hostile project lines; hostile command-line values; hostile guide lines); `scripts/check-docs.py`, `scripts/check-options.py` and `scripts/check-guide.py`. On 67 phone photos of one book (133 pages) the automatic keystone left 130 pages without a vertical correction and lowered the tilt measured afterwards from 0.45 to 0.19 on average. The Auto keystone button was run once in the real window under a virtual display.

**Not verified**: the Auto keystone result judged by eye on more than a few pages and on other books, or on pages with large pictures, tables or very short lines, where it may do nothing or too little; the sliders, the "Settings for" selector and the pencils in the window by hand; Windows, macOS and arm64 by hand; the table pencil only changes how the OCR reads the zone, it does not find cells. On the macOS Intel runner (an experimental job) two PKCS#12 signing tests fail because that runner's OpenSSL refuses RC2-40-CBC; they do not touch these changes.

**Known limits**: the keystone of a page is measured on the original at the settings in use when you press the button; change the cut or the rotation afterwards and press it again. Other limits of pre.40 stand. No checksums are given here: the release workflow computes them (`SHA256SUMS.txt`) when the draft is built.
